name: PGMT
story: Flat-ground trackers struggle when the terrain changes. PGMT adapts diverse whole-body motions to stairs and uneven ground, with locomotion, teleoperation, and fall recovery in one policy.
method: A pretrained tracking and recovery policy learns to fuse motion intent with selected terrain glimpses, while terrain-aware relaxation allows the motion to adapt to the ground.
pipelineAlt: PGMT pipeline: tracking pretraining, perception injection, terrain glimpses, and motion intent fusion for a unified humanoid policy.
thumbnailAlt: PGMT humanoid motion tracking across stairs and outdoor terrain.

name: TAGA
story: Narrow beams, gaps, and sparse footholds leave little room for error. TAGA learns to focus on the terrain that matters next, enabling agile humanoid locomotion with onboard sensing.
method: An active gaze module uses vision, proprioception, and motion commands to select terrain patches, which a cross-attention encoder fuses into the locomotion policy.
pipelineAlt: TAGA architecture: an active gaze module selects a height-scan patch, a visuomotor encoder applies cross-attention, and an action decoder controls the humanoid.
thumbnailAlt: TAGA humanoid traversing gaps, beams, and sparse footholds.

name: KiVi
story: Glare and occlusion can undermine visual locomotion. KiVi combines vision with body sensing so a quadruped can navigate uneven terrain and stay stable when visual information degrades.
method: A dual-branch estimator keeps proprioception as a stable base and uses memory-enhanced visual attention to add terrain information to the locomotion policy.
pipelineAlt: KiVi pipeline: a kinesthetic module estimates body state, a visuospatial module integrates depth images with memory, and both inform the locomotion actor.
thumbnailAlt: KiVi quadruped maintaining locomotion across varied terrain and visual disturbances.
